items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the public health law, in relation to authorizing
institutional dispensers to dispense controlled substances for use off
premises in an emergency situation for at least three days
items.lawCode: Amd §§3342, 3350 & 3351, Art 33 Title 5 Title Head, Pub Health L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S3416

SPONSOR: FERNANDEZ
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the public health law, in relation to authorizing insti-
tutional dispensers to dispense controlled substances for use off prem-
ises in an emergency situation for at least three days

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends the public health law to include hospitals with a full-
time pharmacy, increases the maximum amount of of medication that can be
dispensed to three days, and clarifies that the law includes methadone.

Section 2 changes the language of "addict" to "person with a substance
use disorder."

Section 3 clarifies that methadone may also be dispensed for treatment
of a substance use disorder.

Section 4 sets forth the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

In March of 2022, the Drug Enforcement Agency (DEA) allowed for clini-
cians working in hospitals, clinics, and emergency rooms to dispense 3
days of buprenorphine and methadone (with an exemption approval from the
DEA). However, the NYS Bureau of Narcotic Enforcement (BNE) does not
allow for the same and per BNE regulations (Part 80.75 (b)), only 24
hours of any controlled substance can be dispensed. This bill will allow
NYS BNE to change its regulations to permit 3 days of medication to be
dispensed, matching federal regulations.

Additionally, the bill clarifies that methadone is included in the type
of medication provided and expands who can dispense such medication
beyond just emergency rooms and hospitals without a full-time pharmacy.
Doing so will allow for additional access to these crucial medications
as New York State continues to fight an overdose epidemic.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

TBD

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the ninetieth day after it shall have
become a law; provided, however, that if chapter 466 of the laws of 2024
shall not have taken effect on or before such date then section one of
this act shall take effect on the same date and in the same manner as
such chapter of the laws of 2024 takes effect.

SPONSOR: FERNANDEZ
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the public health law, in relation to authorizing prac-
titioners in institutional dispensers to dispense controlled substances
as emergency treatment for use off premises

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends the public health law to match regulations related to
dispensing controlled substances with the Federal Drug Enforcement Agen-
cy.

Section 2 sets forth the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

In March of 2022, the Drug Enforcement Agency (DEA) allowed for clini-
cians working in hospitals, clinics, and emergency rooms to dispense 3
days of buprenorphine and methadone (with an exemption approval from the
DEA). However, the NYS Bureau of Narcotic Enforcement (BNE) does not
allow for the same as per BNE regulations.  This bill will allow NYS BNE
to change its regulations to match federal regulations regarding the
dispensing of controlled substances for purposes of initiating mainte-
nance treatment, detoxification treatment, or both. Doing so will allow
for additional access to these crucial medications as New York State
continues to fight an overdose epidemic.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

TBD

This act shall take effect on the ninetieth day after it shall have

D.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S3416D

SPONSOR: FERNANDEZ
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the public health law, in relation to authorizing insti-
tutional dispensers to dispense controlled substances for use off prem-
ises in an emergency situation for at least three days and authorizing
practitioners to dispense controlled substances for use in maintenance
or detoxification treatment to an addict or habitual user

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1 amends the public health law to match regulations related to
dispensing controlled substances for purposes of initiating maintenance
or detoxification treatment with the Federal Drug Enforcement Agency.

Section 2 amends the public health law to allow practitioners to
prescribe any III, IV, or V narcotic drug approved by the federal food
and drug administration specifically for use in maintenance or detoxifi-
cation treatment to an addict or habitual user.

Section 3 sets forth the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

In March of 2022, the Drug Enforcement Agency (DEA) allowed for clini-
cians working in hospitals, clinics, and emergency rooms to dispense 3
days of buprenorphine and methadone (with an exemption approval from the
DEA). However, the NYS Bureau of Narcotic Enforcement (BNE) does not
allow for the same as per BNE regulations.  This bill will allow NYS BNE
to change its regulations to match federal regulations regarding the
dispensing of controlled substances for purposes of initiating mainte-
nance treatment, detoxification treatment, or both. Doing so will allow
for additional access to these crucial medications as New York State
continues to fight an overdose epidemic.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

TBD

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the ninetieth day after it shall have

approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 7  Chapter 546
 
       MEMORANDUM filed with Senate Bill Number 3416-D, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT  to amend the public health law, in relation to authorizing
        institutional dispensers to dispense controlled  substances  for
        use  off  premises  in an emergency situation for at least three
        days  and  authorizing  practitioners  to  dispense   controlled
        substances for use in maintenance or detoxification treatment to
        an addict or habitual user"
 
    APPROVED
 
  This  bill  amends  the  Public  Health Law to authorize practitioners
working in an institutional dispenser to dispense controlled  substances
as  emergency  treatment to a patient for use off premises as authorized
by the Drug Enforcement Agency for the purpose of initiating maintenance
treatment, detoxification treatment, or both. The bill  also  authorizes
practitioners to prescribe certain narcotic drugs for use in such treat-
ment programs and makes other technical changes to existing law.
 
  I  support  the  goals  of  this  legislation,  which would provide an
enhanced mechanism in  New  York  to  address  the  opioid  epidemic.  I
proposed  nearly identical legislation in the Fiscal Year 2026 Executive
Budget. However, the bill uses the  term  "addict,"  an  antiquated  and
stigmatizing term for a person with substance use disorder. Accordingly,
the bill should be amended to avoid use of this term.
 
  I  have reached an agreement with the Legislature to enact this change
in the upcoming legislative session. On the basis of this  agreement,  I
am pleased to sign this bill into law.
 
  This bill is approved.                         (signed) KATHY HOCHUL

                                ______

summary: Authorizes practitioners in institutional dispensers to dispense controlled substances as emergency treatment for use off the premises of the institutional dispenser; authorizes practitioners to dispense controlled substances for use in maintenance or detoxification treatment to an addict or habitual user.
title: Authorizes practitioners in institutional dispensers to dispense controlled substances as emergency treatment and authorizes practitioners to dispense controlled substances for use in detoxification treatment
